question: Can causal transition units or already known MTP output-token history improve selection without future router IDs?
repetitions: one deterministic replay per policy/profile, no sweep
resource: same trace per-GPU byte/slot classes, K25 and asynchronous safe publication; no additional GPU allocation
markov_repair: Normalize one-window expected count to heat steady-state units: .5 heat + .5 * (4/.3) predicted. Earlier weak-scale results retained.
token_signal: After verify, outv[a] is the known next input token and last committed window[a] is its preceding token. A 256-entry causal LRU bigram dictionary stores only previously committed actual routed rows. Earlier rejected branches still count as work but cannot train the dictionary.
token_score: Existing heat plus one anticipated routed-row count / .3. No routing or kernels change. No future router information used.
availability_check: Offline assertion validates next known output ID against next window input; actual features use only previous outputs and committed rows.
transfer_model: 12.6 GB/s aggregate pinned reference for initial replay; slower-range sensitivities required for promising follow-up
cost: Report Python selection/update time and predictor payload bytes separately; no invented TG projection. Feature/selection deployment cost must be measured before adoption.
completion: Evaluate both profiles, preserve negative results. Runtime integration only if evidence is competitive or a clearly diagnosed repair is supported.
